# File Drop

> A file input you can also drop files onto. One list of files, either way.

`<slab-file-drop>` · Form · built on `<input type=file>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/file-drop/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/file-drop.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-file-drop
  label="Attachments"
  name="attachments"
  multiple
></slab-file-drop>
```

A drop is held to what the picker would allow: files that don't match `accept` are left out, and without `multiple`, a drop of several files is ignored. A drop has no picker to say what happened, so screenreaders are told how many files were added and how many were left out. Change what they're told with `addedLabel` and `notAcceptedLabel`, functions of the count, and `too-many-label`.

## Keyboard

| Key          | What it does                                         |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Enter, Space | Opens the browser's file picker, as on a file input. |

## Elements

### `<slab-file-drop>`

Import `slab-elements/file-drop.js` to register it.

A file input with no visual styles that files can also be dropped onto, around a native `<input type="file">`, so it is picked from, focused, and read the way one is.

Files dropped anywhere on the host go into the input's own `files`, the same list the picker fills, so there is one list and one source of truth. A drop dispatches "input" and "change" the way picking does.

Validity is the native input's, as with Text Field: `required` is passed through and `valueMissing` is mirrored onto the host.

A drop is held to what the picker would allow. Dropped files that don't match `accept` are left out, and without `multiple`, a drop of more than one file is ignored, as a browser ignores it on a native file input.

A drop has no picker to say what happened, so screenreaders are told: how many files were added, by `addedLabel`, how many were left out for not matching `accept`, by `notAcceptedLabel`, and when a drop of several files was ignored, by `too-many-label`. A drop that adds nothing is told assertively, since it's an error.

With no files, it submits one empty file under its `name`, as a native file input does.

Style it through its parts and through `:state(disabled)`, `:state(drag-over)`, `:state(error)` and `:state(required)`. What the drop target looks like, and how big it is, is left to the styles around it.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                                |
| `accept`           | `string`  |         | Passed to the picker. Dropped files that don't match it are left out.                                                                        |
| `disabled`         | `boolean` | `false` | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted.                |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                             |
| `multiple`         | `boolean` | `false` | Without it, a drop of several files is ignored, as a native file input ignores it.                                                           |
| `name`             | `string`  | `''`    | The name its value is submitted under, as a native control's `name`.                                                                         |
| `required`         | `boolean` | `false` | Makes it invalid while it has no value, as `required` does a native control.                                                                 |
| `too-many-label`   | `string`  |         | What screenreaders are told when a drop of several files is ignored, without `multiple`. "Only one file can be added" in English when unset. |

#### Properties

| Name                            | Type                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `addedLabel`                    | `(count: number) => string` | What screenreaders are told when files are dropped, from how many were added. "1 file added" and so on in English when unset.                                               |
| `notAcceptedLabel`              | `(count: number) => string` | What screenreaders are told when dropped files are left out for not matching `accept`, from how many were. "1 file isn't an accepted type" and so on in English when unset. |
| `files` (read-only)             | `FileList \| null`          | The files chosen or dropped, as a native file input's `files`.                                                                                                              |
| `form` (read-only)              | `HTMLFormElement \| null`   | The form it belongs to, or `null`.                                                                                                                                          |
| `labels` (read-only)            | `NodeList`                  | The `<label>` elements associated with it, as a native control's `labels`: each `<label for>` that names its `id`, and a `<label>` around it.                               |
| `validationMessage` (read-only) | `string`                    | What's wrong, as the validity message says it: the message given to `setCustomValidity()` or `setValidity()`, or else the browser's own. Empty while it's valid.            |
| `validity` (read-only)          | `ValidityState`             | Its `ValidityState`, as a native control's.                                                                                                                                 |
| `willValidate` (read-only)      | `boolean`                   | Whether its validity is checked when its form submits. It isn't while it's disabled or read-only.                                                                           |

#### Methods

| Signature                                                         | Description                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checkValidity(): boolean`                                        | Whether its value is valid. Dispatches "invalid" when it isn't, as a native control's does.                                   |
| `click(): void`                                                   | Clicks it, as a native element's `click()` does.                                                                              |
| `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`                             | Focuses it, or the part of it that takes focus.                                                                               |
| `reportValidity(): boolean`                                       | Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, dispatches "invalid" and shows the validity message, as a native control's does.   |
| `resetValidityFeedback(): void`                                   | Clears the validity feedback without changing `validity`.                                                                     |
| `setCustomValidity(message: string): void`                        | Makes it invalid with a message of your own, or valid again with an empty one, as a native control's does.                    |
| `setValidity(flags?: ValidityStateFlags, message?: string): void` | Sets its validity and message, as `ElementInternals.setValidity()` does, for checks of your own beyond `setCustomValidity()`. |

#### Events

| Name      | Type    | Description                                                                                                        |
| --------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `input`   | `Event` | As the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.               |
| `change`  | `Event` | When the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.             |
| `invalid` | `Event` | When a check finds its value invalid, as a native control's does. Cancel it to leave the validity message unshown. |

#### Slots

| Name          | Type                | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description` | `Element \| string` | Text that describes it, such as a hint or what the validity message means. It's its accessible description. |

#### CSS parts

| Name               | Description                                                    |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`      | Text about the field, and its validity message when it has one |
| `input`            | The input                                                      |
| `label`            | The label                                                      |
| `validity-message` | The validity message, which says why the value is invalid      |

#### CSS states

| Name                | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(disabled)`  | While it's disabled.                                                                                                      |
| `:state(drag-over)` | While the user drags files over it.                                                                                       |
| `:state(error)`     | While it's invalid and its validity message shows, which is once its validity is reported, as when its form is submitted. |
| `:state(required)`  | While it's required, for styles such as an asterisk.                                                                      |
